messages:
maria_gonzalez: Hey team, escalating a customer on Dedicated in a VPC — they hit intermittent 401s for interactive users after SSO cookie rotation. Happens only when users go through our HAProxy L7 edge -> Istio ingress chain. They say curl with the same token succeeds but the browser flow (signed cookie -> frontend -> api) sometimes gets 401s. Repro steps below. Any immediate ideas?

alex_w: Ugh. Do we have any patterns — specific tenants, times, or load?

maria_gonzalez: So far: (1) Only on the Private/Dedicated host that uses HAProxy (customer-managed) in front of our envoy (Istio). (2) It correlates with the SSO refresh window (cookie rotate). (3) When it fails, the API logs show missing/invalid Authorization header at the authz service.

raj_kumar: Can you paste the minimal reproduction steps and a representative request/response?

maria_gonzalez: Repro steps I gave customer:
1) Login via SSO -> signed cookie set (secure, httpOnly)
2) Frontend exchanges cookie for bearer at our token-exchange endpnt and attaches Authorization: Bearer <token> to API calls
3) Trigger SSO rotation (force short TTL or re-login)
4) Some API calls start returning 401s.

Curl that works from our test machine:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJ...valid..." https://private-api.customer.svc/redwood/v1/models
```
Browser request that fails (captured at frontend before envoy):
```
GET /redwood/v1/models
Host: private-api.customer.svc
Authorization: Bearer eyJ...maybe-new-token
Cookie: _sso_sig=....signed...
```
But our authz logs show: "authorization header not found" for requests that fail.

jonathan_s: So the header is present at the frontend but absent by the time it hits ext_authz? That suggests header is being removed or rewritten mid-path. Any gateway config that rewrites Authorization -> X-Forwarded-Authorization?

maria_gonzalez: Customer's HAProxy config had a snippet to preserve original auth on retries and add X-Forwarded-Authorization: they were trying to move the header for an internal shim. I asked for tcpdump at the node and they forwarded one.

carlos_p: Can you paste the tcpdump or envoy access log excerpt?

maria_gonzalez: From the envoy ingress access log (failing request):
```
[2024-07-12T15:02:12.345Z] "GET /redwood/v1/models" 401 - "-" "-" rt=12.3ms ua="curl/7.68.0" auth_error="no_authorization_header"
```
From HAProxy capture (same request just before sending to envoy):
```
Authorization: Bearer eyJ...old-token
X-Forwarded-Authorization: Bearer eyJ...new-token
```
From envoy inbound (what envoy actually receives):
```
X-Forwarded-Authorization: Bearer eyJ...new-token
```
Authorization header missing.
```

raj_kumar: Ahh interesting — HAProxy is sending both, but envoy sees only X-Forwarded-Authorization. I know Envoy (and Istio) will strip certain headers by default or canonicalize them. Also ext_authz filter has a forward_bearer_token option that can be set. If HAProxy intentionally renames Authorization to X-Forwarded-Authorization, we need to ensure envoy is configured to accept that or copy it back.

alex_w: Do we have an Istio EnvoyFilter that removes Authorization for external traffic? Or a header whitelist on the Gateway? Sometimes Gateways have headers_to_remove configured.

maria_gonzalez: Customer's cluster-level Istio Gateway had a text transform that strips hop-by-hop headers; they dropped Authorization because they thought it was sensitive. Their rationale: avoid forwarding creds to upstream internal services. But our auth flow needs Authorization to reach ext_authz.

jonathan_s: Two directions: (A) Ask HAProxy to stop renaming Authorization (preferred). (B) Add an EnvoyFilter to copy X-Forwarded-Authorization -> Authorization before ext_authz runs as a short-term mitigation.

carlos_p: We tried (B) in a dev cluster earlier. Example Envoy Lua snippet we used: 
```
-- Envoy Lua to copy X-Forwarded-Authorization to Authorization if missing
function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
  local auth = request_handle:headers():get("authorization")
  if not auth then
    local xauth = request_handle:headers():get("x-forwarded-authorization")
    if xauth then
      request_handle:headers():add("authorization", xauth)
    end
  end
end
```
Worked for us but is hacky (and latency-sensitive).

raj_kumar: Also confirm ext_authz forward_bearer_token. In Envoy ext_authz v3, you can set forward_bearer_token: true so the filter will forward Authorization header in the check call and not strip it. But if the header is missing in the main request, that won't help.

maria_gonzalez: Customer wants a root cause statement. I drafted: "HAProxy is sending both Authorization and X-Forwarded-Authorization during cookie rotation; Istio/Envoy Gateway is configured to remove Authorization (cluster policy) and not copy X-Forwarded-Authorization back, so downstream ext_authz sees no Authorization header and rejects the request." Thoughts?

alex_w: Sounds accurate. Add evidence: the tcpdump shows both headers, envoy accesslog shows only x-forwarded. Also include the timing (cookie rotate window), because when tokens flip, HAProxy ends up forwarding the new token in X-Forwarded-Authorization while dropping the old Authorization — mismatch leads to authz mismatch.

maria_gonzalez: Customer asked about long-term fix. I proposed:
- HAProxy: stop renaming Authorization. If they need X-Forwarded-Authorization for their internal logic, only add it when Authorization not present.
- Istio: remove the Gateway-level header stripping for Authorization or add a controlled EnvoyFilter that preserves/copies the header before ext_authz.
- Redwood: document guidance for Private customers using HAProxy in front of Istio: do not drop/prefix Authorization; if you need to add X-Forwarded-Authorization, ensure envoy receives Authorization header as well.

jonathan_s: Agreed. Also call out security tradeoffs: preserving Authorization to upstream services is sensitive — customers must ensure that the next hop (our ext_authz and internal services) are trusted. We should add an example EnvoyFilter and a caution in docs.

sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-2024-7345 — dedicated-vpc-haproxy-auth-strip — assigned to eng-platform.

raj_kumar: For an immediate workaround for affected customers: deploy the Lua EnvoyFilter above in the Gateway namespace, and set header whitelist so Authorization is not removed. Command we gave customer to test locally (kubectl apply -f):
```
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: copy-xauth-to-auth
  namespace: istio-system
spec:
  workloadSelector:
    labels:
      istio: ingressgateway
  configPatches:
  - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER
    match:
      context: GATEWAY
      listener:
        filterChain:
          filter:
            name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager
    patch:
      operation: INSERT_BEFORE
      value:
        name: envoy.lua
        typed_config:
          "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
          inlineCode: |
            function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
              local auth = request_handle:headers():get("authorization")
              if not auth then
                local xauth = request_handle:headers():get("x-forwarded-authorization")
                if xauth then
                  request_handle:headers():add("authorization", xauth)
                end
              end
            end
```

jonathan_s: Put a TTL/metrics on it. Also watch for header injection attacks — copying blindly could be abused if HAProxy isn't honest. Put an allowlist for HAProxy source IPs.

maria_gonzalez: Customer rolled the Lua filter in their staging and reported immediate drop in 401s during rotation window. They're planning to update HAProxy to stop renaming Authorization and remove the workaround once stabilized.

alex_w: Nice. Can we fold this into a short KB: "Private/Dedicated: HAProxy -> Istio header rewrite causing Authorization loss / SSO rotation 401s" with: root cause, reproduction, workaround (EnvoyFilter), and long-term fix? I'll take that.

maria_gonzalez: Thanks — filing KB now. Adding logs, tcpdump, and the customer's HAProxy snippet to the KB.

carlos_p: One more note for eng-platform: consider adding a check in our onboarding checklist for Private customers that use HAProxy or L7 proxies in front of Istio: confirm Authorization header preservation or recommend an approved transformation pattern.

maria_gonzalez: Agreed. Closing the thread once KB and patch are merged. :white_check_mark:
